status_summary: A Federal Register search of presidential documents from 2025-01-20 found no mask or vaccine mandate; the vaccine-related orders found direct reinstatement of service members discharged under the military COVID-19 vaccine requirement (Executive Order 14184), set a policy of withholding discretionary federal funds from schools that require COVID-19 vaccination (Executive Order 14214) and issue childhood vaccine recommendations (Executive Order 14420). HHS also rescinded the Head Start COVID-19 mitigation policy requirement (published 2025-12-19). On student loans, no executive loan cancellation was found: the main changes came by statute (Public Law 119-21, which ends Grad PLUS, creates the Repayment Assistance Plan and delays the 2022 borrower defense rule) and a December 2025 agreement to end the SAVE plan, while a 2025 PSLF employer rule was vacated in court (see c11-05 and c11-08).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14184 signed (published 2025-02-03): directs reinstatement offers with back pay for service members discharged over the military COVID-19 vaccine requirement; it states the Defense Secretary had lifted the requirement on 2023-01-10.
Executive Order 14214 signed (published 2025-02-20): sets a policy of withholding discretionary federal funds from schools and colleges that require COVID-19 vaccination for in-person attendance.

Public Law 119-21 is signed. Section 81001 ends Grad PLUS loans and sets new limits for loans from 2026-07-01, section 82001 creates the Repayment Assistance Plan, and section 85001 delays the 2022 borrower defense rule (per CRS).

ED announces an agreement with Missouri to end the SAVE repayment plan, stop new enrollment, deny pending applications and move current borrowers to other plans; it requires court approval, and the release says the agreement itself provides no forgiveness.

HHS publishes a rule rescinding the Head Start COVID-19 mitigation policy requirement (45 CFR 1302.47(b)(9)), effective 2026-02-17 unless significant adverse comments were received; the earlier masking and staff vaccination requirements had already been removed in 2023.
ED publishes final loan regulations implementing Public Law 119-21 (new loan limits, Repayment Assistance Plan, phase-out of other income-driven plans), effective 2026-07-01.
Two federal district courts vacate ED's 2025 Public Service Loan Forgiveness employer rule the day before it took effect; ED appealed on 2026-08-27 (per CRS).
Executive Order 14420 signed (published 2026-08-14): sets childhood vaccine recommendations and directs agency planning; it imposes no vaccination requirement on individuals or institutions.

title: No unilateral mask or vaccine mandates and no arbitrary student loan debt transfers
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c11-05 is in_progress 40 and c11-08 is implemented 75. The objective is a restraint; no new mandate or executive loan cancellation was found, and operative steps align with it (the Head Start rescission, Executive Order 14214, the loan statute and the SAVE agreement), so the combined stage is in_progress 50; the reviewer raised it from 45 once c11-08 was available. Implemented 65 is defensible for the restraint as observed; in_progress 40 if the forgiveness record alone is weighted. Searches: Federal Register API queries for presidential documents with the terms COVID-19 vaccine mandate and mask mandate since 2025-01-20 returned the three vaccine-related orders above and no mask document; a rules query for COVID-19 vaccination requirement returned the Head Start rescission and no other COVID-19 requirement removal. Other rescissions, such as CMS health-facility staff vaccination rules and the Defense Department mandate, took place in 2023 and are not in the window. Federal contractor, federal employee and traveler requirements were not separately confirmed by agency pages, so remaining requirements could exist. Whether the court approved the SAVE agreement was not checked. Whether the Head Start rule took effect on 2026-02-17 was not confirmed: five comments were received, and the effective date applied unless the comments were significant adverse ones. The broader phrase on unilateral mandates of any sort is not measurable here; the administration has issued many executive orders, which this record does not characterize. Executive Order 14214 conditions federal funds on school vaccine policies, which some may view as a unilateral directive; it is described neutrally here. c11-08 is restated because its Repayment Assistance Plan replaces the income-driven plans used for broad forgiveness; it does not itself cover the SAVE agreement. EO 14420 text beyond its Federal Register metadata was not reread by the reviewer.
